requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a single-dimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.
requirements.canonical: For a multi-dimensional port array, the index of the port at which the `getreply` operation was successful MAY be stored in an integer array or record of integer variable.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- It is also possible to store the index of a port in a single-dimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.original: When checking the port array for matching replies, the port indices to be checked are iterated from lowest to highest.
requirements.canonical: When a port array is checked for matching replies, the port indices to be checked ARE iterated from lowest to highest.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- When checking the port array for matching replies, the port indices to be checked are iterated from lowest to highest.

requirements.original: If the port array is multi-dimensional, then the ports are iterated over from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].
requirements.canonical: If the port array is multi-dimensional, the ports ARE iterated over from the innermost to the outermost array dimension, from lowest to highest index for each dimension (e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1]).

readings: The last index varies fastest, as shown by the example sequence [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].
The innermost dimension (first index) is iterated over first, i.e. the first index varies fastest.
ambiguity.issue: 'From innermost to outermost' could be read as the first index varying fastest, but the example sequence shows the last index varying fastest; the canonical follows the example.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- If the port array is multi-dimensional, then the ports are iterated over from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].

requirements.original: The first port which matches all the criteria will cause the operation to be successful even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.
requirements.canonical: The first port of the port array that matches all the criteria CAUSES the `getreply` operation to be successful, even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- The first port which matches all the criteria will cause the operation to be successful even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.

requirements.original: a) A getreply operation shall only be used at a procedure-based port.
requirements.canonical: A `getreply` operation SHALL only be used at a procedure-based port.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- a) A getreply operation shall only be used at a procedure-based port.

requirements.original: The type definition of the port shall include the name of the procedure to which the getreply operation belongs.
requirements.canonical: The type definition of the port at which a `getreply` operation is used SHALL include the name of the procedure (signature) to which the `getreply` operation belongs.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- The type definition of the port shall include the name of the procedure to which the getreply operation belongs.

requirements.original: b) The signature argument of the getreply operation shall not be used to pass in variable names for out and inout parameters.
requirements.canonical: The signature argument of a `getreply` operation SHALL NOT be used to pass in variable names for out and inout parameters.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- b) The signature argument of the getreply operation shall not be used to pass in variable names for out and inout parameters.

requirements.original: c) Parameters or return values of responses accepted by get any reply shall not be assigned to a variable, i.e. the **param and value clause shall not be present.**
requirements.canonical: Parameters or return values of replies accepted by a get any reply operation SHALL NOT be assigned to a variable, i.e. the `param` and `value` clauses SHALL NOT be present.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- c) Parameters or return values of responses accepted by get any reply shall not be assigned to a variable, i.e. the **param and value clause shall not be present.**

requirements.original: d) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause 6.2.9) of the port instance referenced in the getreply operation.
requirements.canonical: All AddressRef items in the `from` clause and all ValueRef items in the `sender` clause of a `getreply` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `getreply` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- d) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause 6.2.9) of the port instance referenced in the getreply operation.

requirements.original: No AddressRef in the from clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.
requirements.canonical: An AddressRef in the `from` clause of a `getreply` operation SHALL NOT contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- No AddressRef in the from clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.

requirements.original: e) The PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized port array.
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef of a `getreply` operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized port array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- e) The PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized port array.

requirements.original: f) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from port array construct.
requirements.canonical: The index redirection of a `getreply` operation SHALL only be used when the operation is used on an `any from` port array construct.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- f) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from port array construct.

requirements.original: g) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective port array.
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a single-dimensional port array, the type of the integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index of the respective port array.
requirements.condition: index redirection is used for a single-dimensional port array
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- g) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective port array.

requirements.original: h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective port array, and the its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the size of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL be exactly the same as the number of dimensions of the respective port array.
requirements.condition: index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array

ambiguity.issue: 'the dimension of the respective port array' means the number of dimensions of the port array.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective port array, and the its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.

requirements.original: h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective port array, and the its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the element type of the integer array or record of integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.
requirements.condition: index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective port array, and the its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.

requirements.original: i) If a variable referenced in the value, param, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the getreply operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the getreply operation.
requirements.canonical: If a variable referenced in the `value`, `param`, `sender` or `@index` clause of a `getreply` operation is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to that variable IS equal to the result produced by the `getreply` operation, and later evaluation of the variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the `getreply` operation.
requirements.condition: the referenced variable is a lazy or fuzzy variable
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- i) If a variable referenced in the value, param, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the getreply operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the getreply operation.

requirements.original: j) If the getreply operation contains both from and sender clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause shall be type compatible with the template in the from clause.
requirements.canonical: If a `getreply` operation contains both a `from` and a `sender` clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause SHALL be type compatible with the template in the `from` clause.
requirements.condition: the getreply operation contains both from and sender clause
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- j) If the getreply operation contains both from and sender clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause shall be type compatible with the template in the from clause.

requirements.original: If the operation contains a sender clause but no from clause, the sender shall be type compatible with the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause.
requirements.canonical: If a `getreply` operation contains a `sender` clause but no `from` clause, the sender SHALL be type compatible with the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause.
requirements.condition: the getreply operation contains a sender clause but no from clause
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- If the operation contains a sender clause but no from clause, the sender shall be type compatible with the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause.

requirements.original: NOTE 3: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.
requirements.canonical: An error due to a type mismatch MAY occur if the types in the receive part of a `getreply` operation are not compatible with the types in the assignment part, or if the `from` clause is missing and the determinable type of the sender is not type compatible with the type in the `sender` clause.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- NOTE 3: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.

requirements.original: k) When assigning implicitly decoded parameters or referenced fields of the return value (by using the @decoded modifier) in cases where the value or template to be matched uses the MatchDecodedContent (decmatch) matching for the parameter to be stored, the type of the template in the MatchDecodedContent matching shall be type-compatible to the type of the variable the decoded field is stored into.
requirements.canonical: When implicitly decoded parameters or referenced fields of the return value are assigned by using the `@decoded` modifier and the value or template to be matched uses `decmatch` matching for the parameter to be stored, the type of the template in the `decmatch` matching SHALL be type compatible with the type of the variable the decoded field is stored into.
requirements.condition: @decoded is used and the matched template uses decmatch for that parameter
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- k) When assigning implicitly decoded parameters or referenced fields of the return value (by using the @decoded modifier) in cases where the value or template to be matched uses the MatchDecodedContent (decmatch) matching for the parameter to be stored, the type of the template in the MatchDecodedContent matching shall be type-compatible to the type of the variable the decoded field is stored into.

requirements.original: l) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `getreply` operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- l) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.original: m) The @nodefault modifier is allowed only in stand-alone getreply statements.
requirements.canonical: The `@nodefault` modifier SHALL only be used in stand-alone `getreply` statements.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.4 -- m) The @nodefault modifier is allowed only in stand-alone getreply statements.

requirements.original: ObjectReference "." raise "(" Signature "," TemplateInstance ")" [ to Address ]
requirements.canonical: The `raise` operation has the syntax ObjectReference "." `raise` "(" Signature "," TemplateInstance ")" [`to` Address].
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- ObjectReference "." raise "(" Signature "," TemplateInstance ")" [ to Address ]

requirements.original: NOTE 1: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "all component"._
requirements.canonical: The Address in the `to` clause of a `raise` operation MAY be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRefs or `all component`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- NOTE 1: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "all component"._

requirements.original: For testing it is allowed to specify a raise operation without an associated getcall operation.
requirements.canonical: For testing, a `raise` operation MAY be specified without an associated `getcall` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- For testing it is allowed to specify a raise operation without an associated getcall operation.

requirements.original: The value part of the raise operation consists of the signature reference followed by the exception value.
requirements.canonical: The value part of the `raise` operation IS composed of the signature reference followed by the exception value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- The value part of the raise operation consists of the signature reference followed by the exception value.

requirements.original: Therefore the exception value may either be derived from a template conforming to the template(value) restriction or be the value resulting from an expression (which of course can be an explicit value).
requirements.canonical: The exception value of a `raise` operation MAY be derived from a template conforming to the template(value) restriction or be the value resulting from an expression.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- Therefore the exception value may either be derived from a template conforming to the template(value) restriction or be the value resulting from an expression (which of course can be an explicit value).

requirements.original: The optional type field in the value specification to the raise operation shall be used in cases where it is necessary to avoid any ambiguity of the type of the value being sent.
requirements.canonical: If it is necessary to avoid ambiguity of the type of the value being sent, the optional type field in the value specification of the `raise` operation SHALL be used.
requirements.condition: the type of the value being sent is ambiguous
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- The optional type field in the value specification to the raise operation shall be used in cases where it is necessary to avoid any ambiguity of the type of the value being sent.

requirements.original: Exceptions to one or more call operations may be sent to one, several or all peer entities connected to the addressed port.
requirements.canonical: An exception to one or more `call` operations MAY be sent to one, several or all peer entities connected to the addressed port.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- Exceptions to one or more call operations may be sent to one, several or all peer entities connected to the addressed port.

requirements.original: This means, the argument of the to clause of a raise operation is for unicast exceptions the address of one receiving entity, for multicast exceptions a list of addresses of a set of receivers and for broadcast exceptions the all component keywords.
requirements.canonical: The argument of the `to` clause of a `raise` operation IS the address of one receiving entity for unicast exceptions, a list of addresses of a set of receivers for multicast exceptions, and the `all component` keywords for broadcast exceptions.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- This means, the argument of the to clause of a raise operation is for unicast exceptions the address of one receiving entity, for multicast exceptions a list of addresses of a set of receivers and for broadcast exceptions the all component keywords.

requirements.original: In case of one-to-one connections, the to clause may be omitted, because the receiving entity is uniquely identified by the system structure.
requirements.canonical: In case of one-to-one connections, the `to` clause of a `raise` operation MAY be omitted.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- In case of one-to-one connections, the to clause may be omitted, because the receiving entity is uniquely identified by the system structure.

requirements.original: a) An exception shall only be raised at a procedure-based port.
requirements.canonical: An exception SHALL only be raised at a procedure-based port.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- a) An exception shall only be raised at a procedure-based port.

requirements.original: b) The type of the exception shall be specified in the signature of the called procedure.
requirements.canonical: The type of the exception raised by a `raise` operation SHALL be specified in the signature of the called procedure.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- b) The type of the exception shall be specified in the signature of the called procedure.

requirements.original: The type definition of the port shall include in its in or inout list the name of the procedure to which the exception belongs.
requirements.canonical: The type definition of the port at which a `raise` operation is used SHALL include in its `in` or `inout` list the name of the procedure (signature) to which the exception belongs.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- The type definition of the port shall include in its in or inout list the name of the procedure to which the exception belongs.

requirements.original: c) A to clause shall be present in case of one-to-many connections.
requirements.canonical: In case of one-to-many connections, a `to` clause SHALL be present in a `raise` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- c) A to clause shall be present in case of one-to-many connections.

requirements.original: d) All AddressRef items in the to clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause 6.2.9) of the port instance referenced in the raise operation.
requirements.canonical: All AddressRef items in the `to` clause of a `raise` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `raise` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- d) All AddressRef items in the to clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause 6.2.9) of the port instance referenced in the raise operation.

requirements.original: No AddressRef in the to clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.
requirements.canonical: An AddressRef in the `to` clause of a `raise` operation SHALL NOT contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- No AddressRef in the to clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.

requirements.original: e) Applying a raise operation to an unmapped or disconnected port shall cause a test case error.
requirements.canonical: Applying a `raise` operation to an unmapped or disconnected port SHALL cause a test case error.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- e) Applying a raise operation to an unmapped or disconnected port shall cause a test case error.

requirements.original: f) The TemplateInstance shall conform to the template(value) restriction (see clause 15.8).
requirements.canonical: The TemplateInstance of a `raise` operation SHALL conform to the template(value) restriction.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- f) The TemplateInstance shall conform to the template(value) restriction (see clause 15.8).

requirements.original: g) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `raise` operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.3.5 -- g) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.
